title: Topic 4 - Compiling Tools
notes: Why build automation: scaling from single‐file compilation to multi‐file projects; error prevention; reproducibility.
The role of make: dependency tracking; selective recompilation; convention over configuration.
Makefile anatomy: targets, prerequisites, recipes; default goal is the first target.
Basic rules: target: deps + tab‐indented commands; example: hello: hello.c → gcc -o hello hello.c.
Variables: CC, CFLAGS, LDFLAGS; assigning with = or :=; using $(VAR).
Pattern rules: %.o : %.c with compile recipe; generic build rules.
Implicit rules & suffix rules; built‐in rules database in make.
Dependency generation with gcc -MMD -MP for C projects.
Recursive make: pitfalls; alternatives with include and directory variables.
Debugging makefiles: make -n, make -d, make -p; tracing variable expansion.
Parallel builds: make -jN; race conditions; order‐only prerequisites.
Include directive: include common.mk; centralizing compiler settings.
Cleaning: adding clean target with rm -f *.o program.
Installing: install target using cp/mkdir; PREFIX variable; DESTDIR for packaging.
Environment variables: exporting vars into recipes; overriding make vars at CLI.
Case study: building multi‐module C project with separate src/, obj/, bin/ directories.
Course usage: simplifying builds for labs; preparing for OS/Compilers courses.
